messages:
support_jess: Hey team — customer on private/VPC deployment reporting a morning spike: a burst of 429s followed by a few 401s. They say billing shows a big token burn. They're using a customer-managed edge proxy in front of our gateway (nginx -> kube ingress -> envoy). Any quick checklist?

customer_ops_tom: I have the customer's basic topology: external NLB -> nginx (edge proxy) -> k8s ingress (contour/Envoy) -> customer-managed gateway -> private control plane. They said the spike correlated with a cron job + a lambda fanout.

alex_sre: First pass checklist: 1) Confirm if the 429s are emitted by our private gateway or upstream proxy. 2) Check auth errors timeline (401) — could be token expiry or clock skew. 3) Inspect rate limiter configs both on customer edge and in private control plane to avoid dual-limiting.

maria_net: Also check nginx limit_req/limit_conn zones and any per-IP limit. If nginx is returning 503/502, it can trigger retries that blow quotas.

eng-platform-raj: From the control plane logs I see 429s with reason=quota_exhausted at 2051112301. Sample gateway log: 
```
ts=2026-03-17T09:05:01Z level=warn component=gateway request_id=abc123 status=429 reason=quota_exhausted route=/v1/generate client_id=acct-987
```
This indicates the token/account hit its per-minute token window.

support_jess: They reported 401s intermittently right after the 429 burst — could those be downstream auth middleware rejecting cached tokens?

alex_sre: Yes, if edge proxy retries with different credentials or strips Authorization header we can see 401s. Suggest repro steps:
1) Run a parallel client flood to gateway endpoint with valid bearer token: `ab -n 500 -c 50 -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://private-gw.example.com/v1/generate`
2) Tail gateway and control plane logs.
3) Compare which component emits 429 vs 401.

maria_net: Also verify kube ingress annotations. Example problematic nginx annotations we've seen:
```
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-connections: "1"
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps: "10"
```
If both nginx and Envoy rate limit similar requests, retries can cascade.

eng-platform-raj: For Envoy native rate limiting + external rate-limit service, confirm the limits are set to allow burst smoothing. Example Envoy descriptor config we recommend:
```
- domain: redwood
  descriptors:
  - key: path
    value: /v1/generate
    rate_limit:
      unit: minute
      requests_per_unit: 600
      burst: 200
```
This gives a leaky-bucket buffer so short spikes don't hit the per-minute cap immediately.

customer_ops_tom: Customer also said their billing showed a sudden token burn exactly at spike time. Could client retries be counting as tokens?

alex_sre: Yes — every successful tokenized call counts. Retries that succeed will increase consumption. Also check if the edge proxy is terminating streaming responses early which might result in replays.

support_jess: Any immediate mitigations we can suggest the customer do while we investigate?

eng-platform-raj: Quick mitigation list: 
- Temporarily raise the account per-minute token quota in the private control plane for that customer (if they have capacity) to buy time.
- Add smoothing/burst allowance in Envoy/native rate limiter as above.
- Disable aggressive retries in nginx (set `proxy_next_upstream` to avoid retry storms).
- Check time sync on all gateway/edge hosts (clock skew can cause tokens to be rejected with 401).

maria_net: Also recommend adding a top-level circuit-breaker on their edge to drop or queue bursts (eg limit_conn + limit_req with burst and nodelay false) so traffic is buffered rather than retried.

sre-bot: alert: spike detected 2051112298 -> peak RPS 450 -> sustained 30s. Tokens consumed +84% minute-over-minute.

alex_sre: For repro add a curl snippet to reproduce 401 pattern:
```
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://private-gw.example.com/v1/generate &
done
wait
```
If you see a mix of 429 then 401, capture the gateway headers `x-rw-rate-limit` and `x-rw-request-id`.

support_jess: Customer tried increasing pod replicas; still saw 429s. Could there be a global token cap enforced downstream?

eng-platform-raj: Yes, our private control plane enforces account-level quota that is independent of pod count. Autoscaling won't help if the quota is saturated. That's where burst smoothing or raising the quota is needed.

customer_ops_tom: Customer is okay with a short quota bump if we can add a guardrail to avoid repeat burn.

alex_sre: Proposed action items: 
- Support team: offer a temporary quota raise and enable rate-limit burst buffer for 1 hour.
- Customer: change edge retry policy and add nginx ingress smoothing annotations.
- Eng-platform: add a telemetry snippet to correlate `x-rw-request-id` across logs and confirm where 401s originate.

support_jess: I'll propose those to the customer and request logs (gateway headers + nginx error log around spike). Thanks all. :thumbsup:

maria_net: If they want a config example for nginx smoothing I can paste one.

support_jess: Please do — that'll help them move fast.

maria_net: Example nginx rate limiting that leans on a shared key and burst window:
```
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=one:10m rate=50r/s;
server {
  location /v1/ {
    limit_req zone=one burst=100 nodelay;
    proxy_pass http://upstream-gateway;
    proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;
  }
}
```
Note: `nodelay` removes queuing; consider removing it to let smoothing happen.

support_jess: Perfect. Sending to customer now and opening a quick internal ticket for quota bump.

eng-platform-raj: I'll also add a short-runner in the control plane to log per-account burst events with the request ids for postmortem.

customer_ops_tom: Customer will run the curl repro and send logs. I'll update the thread when I have them.

support_jess: Closing the loop here once they confirm. Thanks team.
